# The Factorization Display {#sec-factorization}

The theorem of @sec-theorem answers *whether* a scheme exists. This
section gives the display that answers *what the claims admitting an
enduring, computable scheme actually are* — and, in doing so, identifies
two of the paper's three axes with an algebra that predates this paper
by four decades.

::: {.theorem}
**The factorization display** (`factorization_COMP`). At the computable
stratum, enduring flavor: $\Claim$ admits an enduring, offline,
computable evidence scheme **iff**
$$\Claim \in \pstar\big(\Sigma_1 \cap \UpC(\sqsubseteq)\big),$$
i.e. there exists $\psi$ such that $\psi$ is computably semi-decidable,
$\psi$ is upward-closed under $\sqsubseteq$, and $\Claim = \lambda\, w\;
\xi.\ \psi\ w$.
:::

The display is $\TTend(\computable)$ repackaged, and its proof says so:
it rewrites along the biconditional and then discharges two record-side
facts that convert the axes into conditions on $\psi$ —
`determined_eq_proj`, that a determined claim *is* its own record-only
projection, and `monotone_iff_projUpClosed`, that for a determined claim
monotonicity *is* upward-closure of that projection. No new mathematics
is claimed here beyond the theorem being repackaged. What the display
adds is legibility, and three things have to be said about it before
that legibility can be trusted.

## Three readings, none of them free

**(i) The stratum matters.** The identification above is a fact about
the *computable* stratum specifically. At the oracle stratum,
$\pstar(\exists \cdot \mathrm{ALL} \cap \UpC(\sqsubseteq))$ is simply
every upward-closed predicate on records — the Alexandrov topology on
$(\Record, \sqsubseteq)$, with no effectivity content at all. At the
polynomial stratum, $\mathrm{NP} \cap \UpC(\sqsubseteq)$ is not even
closed under the operations that make a frame a frame. The sentence "the
two record-side conditions carve out precisely the effectively-open
sets" is true at exactly one stratum; it is not a general fact about the
three axes restated in topological language.

**(ii) The soundness flavor matters, and the split is this paper's own
contribution within an inherited algebra.** The display covers
*enduring* evidence only. A claim's snapshot-record-side class is
$\Sigma_1$ *simpliciter* — semi-decidable at a fixed stage, with no
upward-closure demanded. This is not a gap in the display; it is the
sharpest sentence available: **snapshot evidence is affirmability of the
finite stage; enduring evidence is observability of the limit.** The
classical tradition's single bundled notion — "observable property,"
meaning simultaneously semi-decidable *and* stable — factors, in this
setting, across the snapshot/enduring distinction, into certifiability
and monotonicity as two independent axes. No source this paper's sweep
reached splits the classical bundle this way (@sec-related-work);
Vickers' polarity distinction splits observable properties along a
different axis entirely — affirmative versus refutative — not along this
one.

**(iii) The algebra is inherited, and credited.** A semi-decidable,
upward-closed set of finite records is exactly a computably-enumerable
union of prefix-cylinders — the *effectively open* sets of the
positive-information topology on records ordered by extension. This is
Escardó's synthetic-topology dictionary, applied: semi-decidable
properties correspond to open sets, and "observable" (Abramsky) or
"affirmable" (Vickers) are the names this tradition already gave them
[@escardo-2004; @abramsky-1987; @vickers-1989], with priority to Smyth's
original topological treatment of predicate transformers
[@smyth-1983]. The class in this setting has finite meets and
*computably-enumerable* joins — the effective form of a frame, not
arbitrary joins — and the honest phrase throughout this paper is "the
effective form of the observables frame," never "a frame" unqualified.

Read together: **at the computable stratum and the enduring flavor, the
claims this paper's theorem admits are exactly the classical frame of
observables pulled back along the projection that forgets context** —
causal history, clocks, key custody, everything a verifier does not see.
Two of the three axes therefore live inside a well-studied algebra, and
the pullback that carries them there is the most elementary frame
homomorphism available; neither is claimed. What is this paper's own is
the third axis — determination, whose entire content is *which* claims
lie in the image of that pullback at all (@sec-related-work) — and the
snapshot/enduring factoring of (ii).

## Why "exactly three," and not some other count

The display can be read as having three moving parts — an existential
over a certificate class, a predicate, and an upward-closure condition —
and it is tempting to conclude that "exactly three axes" follows from
counting them. It does not. The same expression parses into a different
number of parts just as easily: the existential bundles a certificate
with a class, and the floor of @sec-floor is an invisible fifth part the
display does not mention at all. The display's role is to make an
already-proved count *legible*, not to *derive* it.

Exhaustiveness rests entirely on the $\Leftarrow$ direction of
$\TTsnap$/$\TTend$ (@sec-theorem): those three conditions, together, are
shown to *construct* a scheme, and nothing weaker than all three is
shown to suffice. That is the sense in which "exactly three" is a
theorem rather than an editorial choice about how to draw a diagram.
